text:
morgan: Heads-up — I just saw a spike of ~20k 5xx from the gateway between 02:03-02:15 UTC. Root cause looks like a routing rule that pinned a model version that is incompatible with the tenant tokenizer.

morgan: Quick dump of the offending rule (from the audit):
```
match: 
  path: /v1/generate
  headers:
    x-tenant: acme-corp
route_action:
  model_pin:
    alias: redwood/gpt-x
    version: v2.1
    required_compat: tokenizer:v1
```

morgan: The tenant header explicitly asked for tokenizer:v2, so the pinned version fails at decode time. Router should have declined pin or auto-falled back, but it routed anyway. :eyes:

sanjay: Ugh. Is this the rule that came from the console rollout UI?
sanjay: If so we may need a validation step when users create a pin vs. model compatibility matrix.

elaine: I saw similar events in telemetry last month but filtered out as noise. Looks like the compatibility field is optional and wasn't enforced by the route validator.

ryan: Can we make the router evaluate a compatibility predicate before committing the mapping? e.g. if route.required_compat != tenant.tokenizer then treat pin as "incompatible" and apply fallback alias.

morgan: Yeah. Two quick mitigation ideas: 1) add a preflight check to the control plane that rejects pins that claim an incompatible required_compat for well-known tenant profiles; 2) route-time enforcement that demotes pinned model to alias fallback rather than sending request to pinned instance.

elaine: For 2) we should be careful: demotion changes SLO expectations. But I agree it's safer. Also add a warning banner in the console on the rule page so users see the incompatibility before saving.

sanjay: telemetry/alerts: we should add an alert for "pin-compat-mismatch-rate" that fires when >0.5% of requests to a route fail due to compatibility errors within a 5m window. That could catch regressions earlier.

ops-bot: deploybot: new alert created -> pin-compat-mismatch-rate (severity: page)

ryan: On implementation: the routing evaluator lives in gateway-service. I can sketch logic:
```
# pseudo
if rule.model_pin and tenant_profile.tokenizer != rule.model_pin.required_compat:
  log.audit("pin_compat_mismatch", rule_id, tenant_id)
  if router_config.enforce_demote:
    selected_model = find_alias_fallback(rule.alias)
  else:
    selected_model = rule.model_pin # current behavior (unsafe)
```

elaine: Also add a read-only compatibility matrix per model in model-catalog so console validator can check on create. Right now compat metadata is scattered in model manifests.

morgan: I'll file infra ticket and link the telemetry query. Created issue: https://redwood/internal/issue/4823 (model-routing: pin vs compat validation). Putting proposed console banner copy in the issue too.

sanjay: Can someone throw a quick sim in the QA env to reproduce the crash? I want the failing decode stack to attach to the issue.

ryan: On it — will run a synthetic with header x-tenant: acme-corp + rule pin v2.1 and attach logs. ETA 30m.

deploy-bot: deployment started for branch routing/preflight-validate (ryan)

morgan: Thanks. Long-term: we should consider a UX affordance that highlights "pin risk" (e.g., if pinned model requires older tokenizers or quantization that many tenants don't support). Maybe a maturity score.

elaine: Agree. Also add a telemetry dimension that tags requests with "pin_used" so we can correlate cost/latency/quality with pins vs alias.

morgan: Summary: immediate -> enforce demotion in router + alert + ticket 4823. Mid-term -> console validation + model catalog compat page + pin-risk UX.

sanjay: +1

ryan: Will post QA logs in the ticket when done.

morgan: Thanks everyone.
